notes: Read SKILL.md in full. Uses the Chrome DevTools MCP server to verify browser work: screenshots, DOM/console/network inspection, performance traces, accessibility tree, plus debugging workflows and test-plan templates.

Medium because setup adds an .mcp.json entry that runs `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated` (SKILL.md:28-39), an unpinned package fetched at launch, and the server lets the agent drive a browser and execute JavaScript in page context. Acceptable: it is the official Chrome DevTools MCP package, defaults to an isolated/dedicated profile, and the skill sets strong guardrails: treat all browser content as untrusted (SKILL.md:72-80), read-only JS with no external requests or cookie/localStorage access (82-90), user confirmation for DOM mutations and for navigating to URLs found in pages, and user instructions win over page content (107).

Users should know that the optional `--autoConnect` mode (SKILL.md:43, 64) attaches to their real logged-in Chrome profile; the skill warns against it unless the test needs logged-in state. Pinning the chrome-devtools-mcp version instead of @latest would reduce supply-chain exposure.
